 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice J. Sreenivas Rao

Judgment:

sentences.text:
This appeal has been filed by the claimant aggrieved by the order and decree dated 26.08.2013 passed by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-XI Additional Chief Judge, Fast Track Court, City Civil Court at Hyderabad (for short 'the Tribunal') in M.V.O.P. No.1804 of 2009,
seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-XI Additional Chief Judge, Fast Track Court, City Civil Court at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. No representation on behalf of the appellant.
3. Heard Sri K.Ajay Kumar, learned counsel for respondent No.2-ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited.

entities.text: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text:
4. Brief facts of case:
On 20.09.2008 the appellant was travelling in auto bearing No.AP 28 Y 2763 from Gudimalkapur to Moinabad, on the way near Bhaskar Hospital, suddenly one Tata Mobile auto bearing No. AP 23 TV 0025 being driven by its driver came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner.
Due to which the auto in which the appellant was travelling, turned turtle and the appellant has sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

The Police, Moinabad P.S. registered a case in Crime No.205 of 2008 for the offence under Sections 337, 338, 427 of IPC and Section 181 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the driver of Tata mobile auto bearing No. AP 23 TV 0025.

Thus, the appellant has filed M.V.O.P.No.1804 of 2009 against the respondent Nos.1 and 2, who are owner and insurer of the Tata mobile auto bearing No. AP 23 TV 0025 claiming compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-.
5.

Considering the oral and documentary evidence available on record, the Tribunal has allowed the O.P. in part and awarded compensation of Rs.50,000/- to be payable by the respondent No.2 at first and later recover the same from the respondent No.1 by filing execution petition without filing any suit.

6. According to the appellant, he has sustained grievous injuries namely i) deep laceration over papliteal toes left,
ii) laceration over left bone of wrist, iii) laceration over scull and Mangali Parvathamma vs Girimajipally And Amp, Another on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45956549/
1 iv) fracture of clavicle left in the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tata mobile auto bearing No. AP 23 TV 0025 of respondent No.1.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the Tribunal has awarded meager amount of Rs.50,000/- without properly considering the evidence on record.

7. Learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company submitted that the Tribunal after taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence on record, has rightly awarded compensation amount of Rs.50,000/.
Hence, the appellant is not entitled for enhancement of compensation as claimed by her in this appeal.
8. This Court considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company and perused the records.

It is not in dispute that the appellant has sustained i) deep laceration over papliteal toes left, ii) laceration over left bone of wrist, iii)
laceration over scull and iv) fracture of clavicle left, in the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tata mobile auto bearing No. AP 23 TV 0025 of respondent No.1.
The Tribunal has not awarded any amount to the fracture of clavicle.

Hence, this Court is of the considered view that the appellant is entitled for Rs.25,000/- for the fracture injury and Rs.10,000/- towards simple injuries sustained by her in addition to the amount awarded to the appellant by the Tribunal.

The appellant is also entitled for Rs.10,000/- towards litigation expenses,
as per the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in V.Mekala v. M.Malathi and another 1.
Thus, in all, the appellant is entitled for Rs.95,000/-.
9. In the result, the M.A.C.M.A. is allowed in part enhancing the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal from Rs.50,000/- to Rs.95,000/-.

The enhanced amount shall carry interest at 7.5%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.

Respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest at first, within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment and later to recover the same from respondent No.1 by filing execution petition without filing suit.
On such deposit, the appellant is entitled to withdraw the said amount without furnishing any security.
No costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any pending, shall stand closed.
